End (topology)

Words: 47
Topology OurBigBook.com
An end of a noncompact topological space describes a coherent way to escape every compact subset. For a cofinal compact exhaustion, when one exists, K1​⊆K2​⊆⋯, it is represented by nested connected components of the complements. A connected noncompact manifold is disconnected at infinity when it has more than one end.

Orientability

Words: 42
Topology OurBigBook.com
Orientability is the existence of a consistent choice of orientation across a manifold. For a smooth manifold, the transition maps of an oriented atlas have positive Jacobian determinant; for a surface this rules out a Möbius-band neighborhood. The orientable smooth manifold condition is its differentiable formulation.

Non-Hausdorff manifold

Words: 37
Topology OurBigBook.com
A non-Hausdorff manifold is a locally Euclidean topological space for which distinct points need not have disjoint neighborhoods. The real line with two origins is a basic example. Nonseparated algebraic schemes exhibit analogous gluing phenomena, but are not generally topological manifolds.

Stone space

Words: 25
Topology OurBigBook.com
A Stone space is a compact Hausdorff space that is totally disconnected, equivalently a compact Hausdorff space with a basis of clopen sets. The topology on a type space gives an important example.

Tail topology on the natural numbers (τ={∅}∪{{n,n+1,…}:n∈N})

Words: 119 Articles: 1
Topology OurBigBook.com
The nonempty open sets are the upper tails of the natural numbers. Arbitrary nonempty unions select the smallest starting index, and finite intersections select the largest, so these sets form a topology. A map into this space is continuous exactly when the inverse image of every upper tail is open.

Continuous maps between cofinite and tail topologies

Words: 71
Tail topology on the natural numbers OurBigBook.com
For a map f:N→N from the cofinite topology to the tail topology on the natural numbers, continuity is equivalent to every set {n:f(n)≥k} being empty or cofinite. If the image is unbounded, every such set is nonempty and cofinite, so f(n)→∞. If it is bounded, its maximum M exists, and the inverse image of the tail at M forces f(n)=M eventually, with f(n)≤M always. Conversely either condition makes every tail preimage empty or cofinite.

Fell topology

Words: 65
Topology OurBigBook.com
The Fell topology on the closed subsets of a locally compact space has subbasic open sets requiring intersection with an open set or avoidance of a compact set. On a locally compact separable metric space, its sequential convergence says that every convergent subsequence of points from the varying sets has its limit in the limiting set, and every point of the limiting set is approximated by points from the varying sets.

Upper-ray topology on the real line ({∅,R}∪{(a,∞):a∈R})

Words: 66
Topology OurBigBook.com
These sets form a topology: a nonempty union of upper rays is another upper ray, or all of R when their endpoints have no lower bound; a finite intersection of rays has endpoint the maximum of their endpoints. The whole line must be included. The continuous map n↦n from N with the cofinite topology to this space is nonconstant, because each upper ray has cofinite inverse image.

Hyperconnected space

Words: 40
Topology OurBigBook.com
A topological space is hyperconnected if any two nonempty open sets intersect. Every continuous map from a nonempty hyperconnected space to a Hausdorff space is constant: two distinct image points would have disjoint open neighbourhoods whose nonempty inverse images contradict hyperconnectedness. Every infinite set with the cofinite topology is hyperconnected.

Closed cover (X=⋃i​Fi​,Fi​ closed)

Words: 57
Topology OurBigBook.com
A closed cover of a topological space is a family of closed sets whose union is the whole space. A finite closed cover can be used in separation and antipodal arguments: in a metric space, vanishing distance to a closed member means actual membership. Unlike an open cover, a closed cover does not automatically have a partition of unity subordinate to its members.

Partition topology

Words: 80
Topology OurBigBook.com
Given a partition of a set, declare a subset open precisely when it is a union of partition blocks. Arbitrary unions and finite intersections of such unions are again unions of blocks, giving a topology. The quotient map to the block set with its discrete topology pulls that topology back to the original set. For the partition of Z into its two parity classes, the only open sets are the empty set, those two classes, and all of Z.

Finite subsets do not define a topology on an infinite set

Words: 61
Topology OurBigBook.com
On an infinite set, the family consisting of all finite subsets and the whole set need not be closed under arbitrary unions. On Z, the union of the singleton subsets of 2Z is infinite and proper, so this family is not a topology. It must not be confused with the cofinite topology, whose proper open sets have finite complements.

Lower limit topology

Words: 113 Articles: 1
Topology OurBigBook.com
The lower limit topology on R has basis of a topology {[a,b):a<b}. Every such nonempty interval contains a rational, so this topological space is separable. Its topology is finer than the usual Euclidean topology; the one-sided basic neighbourhoods allow its square to have an uncountable discrete antidiagonal.

Sorgenfrey plane

Words: 70
Lower limit topology OurBigBook.com
The Sorgenfrey plane is the product topology on two copies of the Sorgenfrey line. It is separable because Q2 meets every nonempty basic rectangle [a,b)×[c,d). Its antidiagonal {(x,−x):x∈R} is an uncountable discrete subspace: [x,x+ϵ)×[−x,−x+ϵ) meets it only at (x,−x). In a discrete space every dense subset is the whole space, so this subspace is not separable. Thus separability need not pass to subspaces of nonmetrizable spaces.
// Target: analysis.bigb

Symmetric product (Symg(X))

Words: 68
Topology OurBigBook.com
The gth symmetric product of a space X is Symg(X)=Xg/Sg​, where the symmetric group permutes the factors. Its points are unordered g-tuples, with repetitions allowed. If X is a Riemann surface, elementary symmetric functions in local complex coordinates make its symmetric product a smooth complex manifold, including along the locus of repeated points. A collection of disjoint circles in X gives a product torus in this symmetric product.

Extremally disconnected space

Words: 40
Topology OurBigBook.com
A topological space is extremally disconnected when the closure of every open set is open. This concerns open sets, not arbitrary subsets. In particular, a nonisolated singleton in a Hausdorff space is closed but not open, so its closure gives a counterexample to that stronger condition.

Countable complement topology

Words: 93 Articles: 1
Topology OurBigBook.com
The open sets are the empty set and subsets whose complement is countable. On an uncountable set, any two nonempty open sets intersect, so the space is not Hausdorff. On a countable underlying set this topology is discrete. The compact subsets of a cocountable space are finite, regardless of the cardinality of the underlying set.

Compact subsets of a cocountable space

Words: 44
Countable complement topology OurBigBook.com
Only finite subsets are compact in the cocountable topology. An infinite subset contains distinct c1​,c2​,…. The open sets obtained by removing the tails {cj​:j≥n} form an increasing open cover, but every finite selection misses a tail point. Finite sets are compact in every topology.

Locally finite family of subsets ((Ai​)i∈I​)

Words: 56
Topology OurBigBook.com
A family (Ai​) of subsets of a topological space is locally finite if every point has a neighbourhood meeting only finitely many of its members. On a compact space such a family has only finitely many nonempty members. For singleton subsets of a Riemann surface, this is the condition permitting prescribed poles of a meromorphic function without accumulation inside the surface.

Indiscrete topology ({∅,X})

Words: 57
Topology OurBigBook.com
The indiscrete topology on a set X has only the empty set and the whole set as open sets. When X has more than one point it is not a Hausdorff space. For example the quotient topology on R/Q is indiscrete: a nonempty open saturated subset contains an interval and all its rational translates, which cover R.

Triangulation of a surface

Words: 39
Topology OurBigBook.com
A triangulation of a surface decomposes it into triangles meeting along full edges or vertices. On a closed surface, each edge is incident with two triangle faces, so 3F=2E. Euler characteristic connects this local counting relation with the surface's topology.

Pasting lemma for closed subspaces

Words: 45
Topology OurBigBook.com
If a space is the union of finitely many closed subspaces and continuous maps on those subspaces agree on every overlap, they combine into a continuous map on the whole space. For a closed target set, its preimage is a finite union of closed sets.

Cofinite topology

Words: 30
Topology OurBigBook.com
The cofinite topology on a set X consists of the empty set together with every subset whose complement is finite. On an infinite set, any two nonempty open sets intersect.

Hahn-Mazurkiewicz theorem

Words: 47 Articles: 1
Topology OurBigBook.com
A nonempty Hausdorff space is the continuous image of [0,1] exactly when it is compact, connected, locally connected, and second-countable.

Peano continuum

Words: 27
Hahn-Mazurkiewicz theorem OurBigBook.com
A Peano continuum is a compact, connected, locally connected metric space. By the Hahn-Mazurkiewicz theorem, every Peano continuum is the image of a continuous surjection from [0,1].

Topological manifold

Words: 5k Articles: 103
Topology OurBigBook.com
A topological n-manifold is a Hausdorff second-countable space in which every point has a neighborhood homeomorphic to an open subset of Rn.

Piecewise linear ball (Bn)

Words: 79 Articles: 1
Topological manifold OurBigBook.com
A piecewise linear ball is a simplicial complex admitting a homeomorphism to an n-simplex that is linear on the simplexes of suitable finite simplicial subdivisions. Its boundary is a piecewise linear sphere.

Gluing three-balls along a boundary disk

Words: 52
Piecewise linear ball OurBigBook.com
Two piecewise linear balls of dimension three glued along a common boundary disk form another piecewise linear ball. The Schoenflies theorem identifies each boundary pair with a sphere and a hemisphere. Coning the resulting boundary homeomorphisms extends them over the balls, which then become the two halves of a standard ball. The same argument shows that removing a ball attached along one boundary disk leaves a ball.

4-manifold (dimM=4)

Words: 218 Articles: 7
Topological manifold OurBigBook.com

Smooth four-manifold

Words: 218 Articles: 6
4-manifold OurBigBook.com
A smooth four-manifold is a four-dimensional smooth manifold. Its intersection form and gauge-theoretic invariants impose strong constraints on its possible smooth and symplectic structures.
Fiber sum of four-manifolds (X#C​Y)
Words: 110 Articles: 1

Topological manifold OurBigBook.com
Glue two copies of a compact manifold along their boundaries to form its double. A collar gives the double a smooth structure when W is smooth. Folding the copies onto W gives a retraction; in particular, inclusion of either copy is injective on homology. For an oriented manifold, use the opposite orientation on the second copy.

Topological tripod

Words: 55
Topological manifold OurBigBook.com
Three intervals joined at one endpoint form a compact connected metric space. It is second countable, Hausdorff and paracompact, but is not a topological manifold. At regular arm points a putative manifold has dimension one; deleting the junction from a small neighborhood instead gives three components, incompatible with an interval chart. This local obstruction precedes any question about a smooth structure.

Invariance of domain

Words: 43
Topological manifold OurBigBook.com
Invariance of domain says that a continuous map that is an injective function between topological manifolds without boundary of the same dimension is an open map. It is useful in the Penrose singularity theorem: projecting a compact achronal boundary along timelike curves onto a Cauchy hypersurface gives a nonempty subset that is both open and closed, forcing that connected Cauchy hypersurface to be compact.

Topological manifold OurBigBook.com
A smooth manifold carrying a nondegenerate bilinear form on each tangent space, with one negative and all remaining positive eigenvalues, or the overall reversed-sign convention. Its nonzero null vectors have vanishing metric quadratic form.

Metric signature ((−,+,+,+))

Words: 47
Lorentzian manifold OurBigBook.com
The metric signature records the signs of the diagonalized nondegenerate metric tensor, equivalently its numbers of negative and positive directions. For a four-dimensional Lorentzian manifold, both (−,+,+,+) and its overall negative convention are common. The numerical signs of contractions and component Hodge star operator identities must be consistent with that choice and the orientation.

Spacelike submanifold

Words: 47
Lorentzian manifold OurBigBook.com
In metric signature (−,+,…,+), a spacelike submanifold of a Lorentzian manifold has an induced metric tensor defining a positive-definite quadratic form. With the overall reversed metric signature, its induced metric tensor instead has only negative eigenvalues. The definition applies to any dimension: enclosing charge-integration surfaces in four dimensions are two-dimensional examples, whereas a spacelike Cauchy hypersurface in four dimensions is three-dimensional.

Handle decomposition OurBigBook.com
Attach two one-handles to a four-dimensional zero-handle, then a two-handle along the commutator of their generators with the product zero framing. The result is T2×D2. Normal surface

Words: 251 Articles: 4
3-manifold OurBigBook.com
Relative to a triangulation, a normal surface meets every tetrahedron in disjoint normal disks: four types of triangles cutting off vertices and three types of quadrilaterals separating opposite pairs of edges. A normal disk meets any edge at most once; its face arcs join distinct edges. Two different quadrilateral types cannot coexist in a tetrahedron.
Normal surface coordinates (x∈Z≥07t​)
Words: 200 Articles: 3
Normal surface OurBigBook.com
For t tetrahedra, count the seven disk types in each tetrahedron. Across each glued face the counts of each of its three normal arc types must agree. These are homogeneous linear equations with integer coefficients. An admissible solution also has at most one nonzero quadrilateral type in each tetrahedron. Matching the arcs in their boundary order reconstructs the normal surface up to an isotopy preserving the tetrahedra.

Words: 53
Normal surface coordinates OurBigBook.com
The weight of a normal surface counts its intersections with the edges of the triangulation. It is a positive linear function of its coordinates: each corner of a normal disk contributes the reciprocal of the number of tetrahedral sectors around its edge. Thus a nontrivial decomposition into compatible coordinate vectors gives both summands strictly smaller weight.

The Haken sum of compatible normal surfaces is obtained by resolving their intersection curves in the way that preserves the normal disk types. A fundamental normal surface has a nonzero admissible coordinate vector which is not the sum of two nonzero admissible vectors. Fixing the allowed quadrilateral type in every tetrahedron reduces the problem to the Hilbert basis of a rational cone. There are finitely many choices of quadrilateral types and finitely many indecomposable vectors for each choice.

Words: 131 Articles: 1
3-manifold OurBigBook.com
A punctured three-sphere is S3 with the interiors of finitely many disjoint piecewise linear balls removed. Capping its spherical boundary components with balls restores S3. Removing another ball or gluing two such manifolds along one spherical boundary component preserves this class.
Sphere surgery preserving nontrivial complementary pieces
Words: 94
Punctured three-sphere OurBigBook.com
Suppose disjoint separating spheres cut a 3-manifold into pieces none of which is a punctured three-sphere. Compress one sphere along a disk disjoint from the others. The old sphere and the two new spheres enclose a three-times punctured sphere. At least one of the two pieces on the compressed side is not a punctured sphere; retain that new sphere and discard the other. The piece on its opposite side cannot become a punctured sphere, since capping its boundaries and applying the Three-dimensional Schoenflies theorem would make the original opposite piece a punctured sphere as well. Hence the number of spheres and the nontriviality condition can be preserved.

Loop theorem

3-manifold OurBigBook.com
If a boundary surface inclusion has noninjective fundamental group map, there is a compression disk whose boundary represents a nontrivial element of that kernel. More generally the boundary can be required to avoid a prescribed normal subgroup if a singular disk with that property exists.
Tower proof of the loop theorem
Words: 85
Loop theorem OurBigBook.com
Start with a singular disk whose boundary represents a prescribed nontrivial class in a boundary subsurface. Repeatedly lift it through double covering spaces of regular neighbourhoods of its image. The number of distinct image simplexes strictly increases and is bounded by the number of domain simplexes, so the tower ends. At the top, vanishing first mod-two homology forces every boundary component to be a sphere. An embedded disk can then be constructed and projected down the tower. Resolving double curves preserves a boundary class outside a chosen normal subgroup, giving an embedded compression disk at the bottom.

For the usual regular complex structure, its holomorphic disk count modulo translation is ±1. For a bigon the Riemann map to the strip is unique up to translation. For a rectangle, the tautological correspondence represents the disk in the symmetric product by a branched double cover of the strip onto the rectangular domain: its conformal modulus fixes the branch parameter, and the only remaining freedom is translation. The resulting isolated regular disk gives one point in the oriented moduli space. The differential coefficient is ±Unz​, so a basepoint-free domain contributes a unit.

A topological space is sober when every nonempty irreducible closed subset is the closure of a unique point. Every Hausdorff space is sober. In contrast, an infinite set with the cofinite topology has the whole space irreducible and closed, while every singleton is closed, so it is not sober.

This is a thickening of the gluing graph, so it is homotopy equivalent to that graph. Thus its Euler characteristic is n−e and its fundamental group is the free group Fe−n+1​. If the gluing graph is a tree, the assembled surface is itself a closed disc.
Suppose each pairing preserves the positive boundary parameter of the reference discs. A global orientation must then assign opposite orientation signs to adjacent tiles, because their induced boundary orientations on an interior seam must oppose one another. Such signs exist exactly when the gluing graph is bipartite. An odd gluing cycle therefore proves that the assembly is a nonorientable surface. A Dirichlet boundary condition or a Neumann boundary condition on an unpaired arc has no effect on this topological calculation.

A one-sided section loop and a two-sided fiber loop in the reflection mapping torus have mod-two self-intersections one and zero and meet once. Their intersection form is Q. In the evaluation-dual cohomology basis, the Poincare duality pairing has matrix Q−1, giving t2=0 and x2=tx=0.

Integral cohomology ring of the Klein bottle (H∗(K;Z))

Words: 105 Articles: 1
Klein bottle OurBigBook.com
The integral cohomology groups of the Klein bottle are H0(K;Z)=Z, H1(K;Z)=Z, H2(K;Z)=Z/2, and zero in higher degrees. The degree-one generator is pulled back from the base circle of the circle-bundle presentation, so its square is zero; hence every product of positive-degree classes vanishes.
Integral cohomology ring of the wedge of the real projective plane and a circle (H∗(RP2∨S1;Z))
Words: 53
Integral cohomology ring of the Klein bottle OurBigBook.com
The wedge RP2∨S1 has the same additive integral cohomology as the Klein bottle: Z in degree zero, Z in degree one, and Z/2 in degree two. Products of positive-degree classes vanish because the degree-one class comes from the circle summand, so its cohomology ring is isomorphic to that of the Klein bottle.

Orientation double cover of the Klein bottle

the transformations with even c form an index-two translation subgroup. Its quotient is a torus, giving the orientation double cover T2→K.
Klein-bottle mapping-cylinder obstruction to simple connectivity
Words: 55
Orientation double cover of the Klein bottle OurBigBook.com
Let Y be the mapping cylinder of the orientation double cover T2→K with its free end omitted. If a Hausdorff space contains Y as an open subset, van Kampen extends the orientation quotient of π1​(K) to a surjection of the ambient fundamental group onto C2​. The ambient space is therefore not simply connected.

Flat Klein-bottle geodesic model

Words: 36
Klein bottle OurBigBook.com
In a flat fundamental square, straight horizontal, vertical and rational-slope lines project to closed geodesics. The central horizontal glide axis is one-sided, a vertical line is two-sided, and the line (2t,t) closes with one transverse self-intersection.

Double cone singularity

Words: 19
Topological surface OurBigBook.com
The vertex of a double cone is not a surface point because its punctured neighborhood disconnects into two pieces.

Knaster-Kuratowski-Mazurkiewicz lemma

Words: 110 Articles: 3
Topology OurBigBook.com
For a simplex with vertices indexed by 0,…,n, let closed sets Fi​ have the property that every face spanned by an index set I lies in ⋃i∈I​Fi​. Then ⋂i=0n​Fi​ is nonempty. The triangle KKM lemma is a two-dimensional covering formulation of this simplex-intersection principle.

Triangle KKM lemma

Words: 66 Articles: 2
Knaster-Kuratowski-Mazurkiewicz lemma OurBigBook.com
If three closed sets cover a triangle and respectively contain its three opposite sides, then their triple intersection is nonempty.

Distance-function barycentric map

Words: 26
Triangle KKM lemma OurBigBook.com
Normalized distances to three closed sets give continuous barycentric coordinates; a covering forces at least one coordinate to vanish, placing the image on the simplex boundary.

No-retraction covering principle

Words: 20
Triangle KKM lemma OurBigBook.com
A closed-cover intersection statement for a simplex is equivalent to the nonexistence of a boundary-valued map that preserves every face.
